discoveries.title: Bathurst Island Group and Byam Martin Island, Arctic Canada (operation Bathurst Island)
creator: J W Kerr
discoveries.context_excerpt: The Bathurst Island group, and Byam Martin Island, together occupy about 8,000 square miles of land area. They are situated near the geographic center of the Canadian Arctic Archipelago and encompass the north magnetic pole. Most of the area is covered by sedimentary rocks of Ordovician to Late Devonian age, with a composite exposed thickness of approximately 20,000 feet. Exposures of younger rocks are limited to small areas in the northwest and southeast. discoveries.context_excerpt: This chapter covers the beginning of Black Gold's racing career at the Fair Grounds in New Orleans. After discussing his impact on the early season juvenile racing at the track, it describes his maiden victory and the odd events surrounding his second race, and introduces one of his major rivals during his two-year-old season, Worthmore. It concludes by introducing the theme of Black Gold's persistent bad luck and the question of its equally persistent appearance in races in which Worthmore was involved.
